problem: "Static power decides whether a chip can sit idle without draining its battery" is ambiguous. Every chip drains its battery while idle; static power decides how fast.
fix: "Static power decides how long a chip can stay idle on one battery charge."

problem: The phrase "the brief time in a switching input when both nMOS and pMOS are on" is garbled and does not say when both devices are actually on.
fix: "Short-circuit power comes from the brief time during an input transition when the input voltage is between the nMOS threshold Vt and VDD − |Vtp|; in that window both the nMOS and the pMOS are on and current flows straight from VDD to ground."

problem: "Lowering VDD ... also lowers static power for a given leakage current" is true only as P = VDD Ileak with Ileak held fixed. A student may read it as "lower VDD and leakage power drops", but in practice keeping speed at lower VDD needs a lower Vt, which raises subthreshold leakage sharply.
fix: "Lowering VDD reduces the switching term as VDD² and, for the same leakage current, reduces static power in proportion to VDD. In practice a lower VDD usually comes with a lower Vt to keep speed, and the lower Vt raises subthreshold leakage far more than the VDD reduction saves."
